```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 7
    n_vehicles = 4
    Q = 38  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[41, 26], [91, 28], [85, 16], [62, 82], [60, 80], [17, 86], [65, 47]]
    demands = [16, 11, 19, 8, 17, 16, 14]
    time_windows = [[0, 317], [31, 110], [46, 115], [65, 158], [33, 119], [41, 123], [62, 136], [40, 130]]
    service_times = [10, 10, 6, 11, 6, 5, 7]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Routing and Scheduling Plan for Customer Deliveries

Overview
We operate a fleet of identical delivery vehicles from a single central depot. For the upcoming planning horizon, all vehicles will depart the depot at time 0, each vehicle will execute a single outbound-and-return route, and all vehicles must return to the depot before the depot’s latest allowable time. Our service area consists of a defined set of customer locations with known coordinates. The travel time between any two locations equals the straight-line distance between their coordinates, with distance units aligned to time units.

Delivery Challenge
We must construct a set of routes that visits every customer exactly once while coordinating departures, arrivals, and returns within the planning horizon. The sequencing of stops must account for travel distances, customer time windows, and on-site service durations, ensuring that each delivery starts within the customer’s acceptable window. If a vehicle reaches a customer location before the window opens, the vehicle will wait on site until service can begin. After service is completed, the vehicle departs immediately, subject to the timing rules below.

Operating Requirements
- Single trip per vehicle: Each deployed vehicle leaves the depot at time 0, visits an ordered sequence of customers, and returns to the depot before closing. No mid-route returns or second trips are permitted.
- Time windows: Each customer has a specified earliest and latest start time for delivery. The delivery must begin within this window. Early arrivals must wait; late starts are not permitted.
- Service times: Every customer has a required unloading/service duration. Vehicles depart a customer at arrival time plus service time (or window open plus service time if they arrived early and waited).
- Capacity and demand: Each vehicle has a limited carrying capacity. The total customer demand assigned to any single route must not exceed this capacity. Deliveries cannot be split across vehicles; each customer is served by exactly one vehicle on exactly one route.
- Fleet and deployment: Vehicles are identical and interchangeable. Deploying a vehicle entails a fixed cost that is incurred in addition to costs associated with distance traveled. Only as many vehicles as needed should be deployed, within the available fleet.
- Travel times and distances: Movement between the depot and customer locations, and between customers, is measured by straight-line distances on the map. Because distance units and time units are aligned, these distances also determine travel times.

Cost Considerations
We seek a routing plan that balances route length, time window feasibility, and capacity utilization against fixed deployment costs. Using additional vehicles can reduce route distances and waiting, but increases fixed costs. Consolidating customers onto fewer vehicles can reduce fixed costs but risks longer routes, more waiting, and time window violations. The plan should strike the right balance while ensuring all customers are served on time and all vehicles return before the depot closes.

Goal
Identify a set of feasible routes—one per deployed vehicle—that:
- Visits every customer exactly once
- Respects all customer time windows and service durations
- Keeps the total demand on each route within vehicle capacity
- Ensures all vehicles depart at time 0 and return to the depot before the depot’s latest time
- Minimizes the sum of total travel distance and vehicle deployment costs

  - C7: 14 units
